A convex lens with a small upright object arrow placed between the focal point F and the lens. Rays from the top of the object diverge after passing through the lens. Dashed lines trace these rays backwards to meet and form a much larger, upright virtual image arrow behind the object. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Two eyeball diagrams for Myopia. Top: Parallel rays from infinity enter the eye and cross (converge) before reaching the retina, leaving a blurred circle on the back of the eye. Bottom: A concave lens is placed in front of the eye. The parallel rays diverge slightly as they pass through it, so the eye lens now brings them to a sharp focus exactly on the retina. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
